01.actor: A man who sold his property intending to move to Eretz Yisrael
01.event: He sold his property while privately intending to ascend to Eretz Yisrael, said nothing at the time, did not go, and wanted to cancel the sale.
01.turn: Rava ruled that an unspoken intention is not binding.
01.outcome: The ruling stands as stated; the passage then moves into a series of failed attempts to find Rava's source.
01.summary: A man sold his property meaning to move to Eretz Yisrael but never said so. When he did not go, he tried to back out of the sale. Rava ruled that thoughts left in the heart are not legally binding.
01.missing: The text does not say how the dispute ended, and nothing after the ruling is narrative; the remaining segments are source-hunting for Rava's principle.

02.event: At his son's wedding Rava poured drinks for guests; two Sages stood for him and two (Rav Mari and Rav Pineḥas) did not.
02.turn: Rava became angry that those two refused to honor him.
02.outcome: He rebuked them for treating some Sages as Sages and others as not.
02.summary: Rava was serving drinks at his son's wedding. When he poured for Rav Pappa and Rav Huna they stood up for him, but Rav Mari and Rav Pineḥas stayed seated. Rava got angry and demanded whether the ones who stood were Sages and they were not.

03.event: A groom complained he found no blood on his wedding night and the bride said she was from the Dorketi family, who have no such blood; Rabban Gamliel checked her relatives.
03.outcome: He told the groom to take his purchase and congratulated him on marrying into the Dorketi family.
03.summary: A man came to Rabban Gamliel the Elder saying he had found no blood with his bride. She said she was from the Dorketi family, whose women have neither menstrual nor hymen blood. Gamliel investigated her relatives, found it true, and told the groom to go keep his bride, saying he was fortunate.

04.event: Rabbi Akiva picked an etrog on the first of Shevat and separated two tithes from it, one by Beit Shammai's rule and one by Beit Hillel's.
04.turn: The Gemara reads it as proof that Beit Shammai acted on their view.
04.outcome: Nothing narrative; it is cited as evidence in a legal argument and the Gemara answers it in a later segment.
04.summary: Rabbi Akiva once picked an etrog on the first of Shevat and tithed it twice, once according to Beit Shammai's new year for trees and once according to Beit Hillel's.
04.missing: No reason or reaction is narrated in the event itself; the explanation is supplied by later legal discussion.

05.actor: Rav Yehuda and the residents of a shepherds' village
05.event: A narrow inlet of the sea breached the wall of a courtyard in a shepherds' village and the matter came before Rav Yehuda.
05.turn: Rav Yehuda required only one upright board of wall to remain.
05.outcome: He permitted the courtyard with a single board; the case is cited as an unresolved precedent.
05.summary: In a shepherds' village the sea cut into a courtyard and breached a whole wall. The case went to Rav Yehuda, who required only one remaining upright board to permit the courtyard.
05.missing: The case is reported only as a precedent in a legal argument; the people involved and any further result are not described.

06.event: A man came to Rabbi Ami claiming another man was a priest because he was called first to the Torah in synagogue.
06.turn: Rabbi Ami questioned whether he was called as a priest or as a prominent person, and the man answered that a Levite read after him.
06.outcome: Rabbi Ami accepted the testimony and elevated the man to priesthood.
06.summary: A man told Rabbi Ami that another man had established the presumption of being a priest by reading first in synagogue. Rabbi Ami asked whether this was due to priesthood or prominence. When the man replied that a Levite read after him, Rabbi Ami accepted the testimony and raised him to the priesthood.

07.actor: Mari bar Isak (or Ḥana bar Isak) and his claimed brother
07.event: A man from Bei Ḥoza'a claimed to be Mari's brother and demanded a share of their father's estate; Mari said he did not know him, and the claimant went to Rav Ḥisda.
07.turn: Rav Ḥisda sided with Mari's denial, then told Mari to bring witnesses that the man was not his brother, because the claimant's witnesses feared Mari.
07.outcome: Rav Ḥisda put the burden of proof on the violent Mari and rejected his protest.
07.summary: A man arrived from a far district claiming to be Mari's brother and asked for a share of the inheritance. Mari said he did not recognize him, so the man took the case to Rav Ḥisda, who at first agreed Mari could fail to recognize him. When the claimant said his witnesses feared Mari, Rav Ḥisda ordered Mari to bring witnesses that the man was not his brother, overriding his objection.

08.event: As he lay dying he tricked the Angel of Death into showing him his place in paradise, took the angel's knife, and leapt into paradise.
08.turn: The Angel of Death grabbed his cloak; he swore not to return, and Heaven ruled he need not go back because he had never annulled an oath.
08.outcome: He kept his place; the knife was returned on a Divine Voice's order and Elijah announced his arrival; in paradise he met Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai.
08.summary: When Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi was dying, the Angel of Death was sent to do his bidding and agreed to show him his place in paradise. He borrowed the angel's knife for safety, then jumped into paradise. The angel grabbed his cloak, but he swore not to come and Heaven let him stay since he had never annulled an oath. Elijah announced his arrival and Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai questioned him about a rainbow.

09.event: He went to study Torah with Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua, but the students there ganged up on him like fighting roosters.
09.turn: They would not let him learn.
09.outcome: He managed to learn only a single teaching, that Rabbi Eliezer holds one is liable to stoning for a hermaphrodite.
09.summary: Rabbi once went to study under Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua. His students banded together against him like aggressive roosters and did not let him learn. He came away with only one teaching from the mishna.

10.actor: A man who made a conditional divorce, and Shmuel
10.event: A man said his bill of divorce would take effect if he did not return within thirty days; he arrived at the end of thirty days but a ferry kept him from crossing, and he called out to people that he had come.
10.turn: Shmuel judged whether shouting across the river counted as returning.
10.outcome: Shmuel ruled that this was not a return, so the condition was fulfilled and the divorce took effect.
10.summary: A man told agents holding his bill of divorce that it would take effect if he did not come back within thirty days. He reached the river on the last day but was stuck on the far side, calling out that he had come. Shmuel ruled that this did not count as returning.

11.event: While visiting villages he was asked whether one may make an eiruv with moist beans and had no answer.
11.turn: Back at the study hall, he was told Rabbi Yannai's ruling.
11.outcome: The answer was that one may, with a handful.
11.summary: Rabbi Yirmeya went out to some villages, and the villagers asked whether an eiruv could be made with moist beans. He could not answer. Back at the study hall he was told that Rabbi Yannai permits it, with a handful as the measure.

12.actor: Rav Ḥiyya Arikha and his brother's widow (his mother-in-law)
12.event: After supporting her for twenty-five years in her father's house, he refused her demand for sustenance and then her marriage contract; she sued him before Rabba bar Sheila.
12.turn: Rabba bar Sheila ruled she could collect, Rav Ḥiyya ignored him, and Rabba issued a document of authorization to seize his property; Rava then confirmed the judgment but found the document defective.
12.outcome: She lost her claim to the produce because the authorization was badly written, since Rabba bar Sheila had erred in leaving out the clause identifying the husband's property.
12.summary: Rav Ḥiyya Arikha supported his brother's widow for twenty-five years, then refused her demands for sustenance and her marriage contract. She sued, and Rabba bar Sheila ordered him to pay her. When he refused, Rabba gave her a seizure order. Rav Ḥiyya appealed to Rava, who upheld the ruling, but when the woman claimed the produce Rava found the order was defective and rejected her claim.

13.actor: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba and Rav
13.event: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba saw Rav recite kiddush early and asked whether he had separated from work, and Rav said yes.
13.turn: Rav confirmed he had accepted the sanctity of the day.
13.outcome: The exchange is cited as legal proof that reciting kiddush early commits one to Shabbat restrictions.
13.summary: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba saw Rav reciting kiddush before Shabbat began and asked if he had therefore stopped working. Rav answered that he had.
13.missing: It is a bare exchange cited as proof; no setting, consequence or resolution is given.

14.actor: Rava and Rav Mari bar Raḥel
14.event: Rava ruled that Rav Mari bar Raḥel, whose father was a gentile and mother Jewish, was fit to marry into Israel and appointed him an official of Babylonia.
14.turn: The verse requiring officials be from among your brethren seemed to bar him.
14.outcome: Because his mother was Jewish, he counted as from among your brethren.
14.summary: Rava declared Rav Mari bar Raḥel, born of a gentile father and Jewish mother, fit to marry into the community and appointed him an official of Babylonia. Though a verse limits such posts to one's brethren, Rava held that his Jewish mother made him qualify.
14.missing: It reports a legal ruling and its justification, with little scene or action.

16.actor: A man's orphaned heirs, his daughter, Rav Yosef and Abaye
16.event: A man declared a palm tree for his daughter; after his death the heirs divided the estate and gave her none.
16.turn: Rav Yosef thought it was like the mishna where each heir can deflect her, but Abaye distinguished it since the tree is held by all of them.
16.outcome: Abaye ruled that they must give her a palm tree and redo the division.
16.summary: A man said he was leaving a palm tree to his daughter, but after his death the heirs split the estate without giving her one. Rav Yosef thought she had no claim, as in the mishna. Abaye answered that here the tree is in their joint possession, so they must give her one and divide the estate again.
16.missing: This is a case stated for a legal ruling; the daughter's actual outcome is not narrated.

17.event: When he was dying he asked the Angel of Death for thirty days to review his learning, then asked to be shown his place in paradise and for the angel's knife.
17.turn: The Angel of Death refused, mentioning what happened with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and Rabbi Ḥanina was questioned on whether he had studied with those suffering from ra'atan.
17.outcome: He died, and a pillar of fire separated him from everyone, a sign of great honor; it left only when Rabbi Alexandri said to do so in his own honor.
17.summary: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa was friends with the Angel of Death. When his time came he got thirty days to review his learning, then asked to be shown his place in paradise and for the angel's knife. The angel refused, citing Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's trick. When Ḥanina died a pillar of fire separated him from the world, and it vanished only when Rabbi Alexandri asked it to go for Ḥanina's own honor.

18.actor: Dama ben Netina, a gentile of Ashkelon
18.event: The Sages wanted to buy merchandise from him at a huge profit, but the key was under his sleeping father's head and he would not wake him.
18.turn: He gave up the large profit out of honor for his father.
18.outcome: The next year a red heifer was born in his herd; when the Sages came he asked only for the money he had lost honoring his father.
18.summary: Dama ben Netina, a gentile in Ashkelon, was asked by the Sages to sell merchandise for a huge profit. The key lay under his sleeping father's head, so he refused to disturb him. The next year a red heifer was born in his herd, and when the Sages came he asked only for the amount he had lost.

19.actor: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ashi and his wife
19.event: His wife wondered why he prayed against the evil inclination after years of abstaining from her; she then disguised herself as the prostitute Ḥaruta and he propositioned her in his garden.
19.turn: At home he sat in the burning oven, confessed, and she revealed it had been her.
19.outcome: He did not initially believe her; once she proved it he said he still had intended to sin, and he fasted until his death.
19.summary: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Ashi prayed daily to be saved from the evil inclination, and his wife wondered why since he was old. One day she dressed up and passed by his garden as a prostitute, and he propositioned her and fetched a pomegranate for her. At home he sat in the burning oven and confessed. She said it was her, but he said he had still intended to sin and fasted for the rest of his life.
19.missing: The wife's reason for disguising herself is implied, not stated.

20.actor: Seven teachings and their unnamed carrier
20.event: Seven teachings said on Shabbat morning before Rav Ḥisda in Sura were repeated near the end of that Shabbat before Rava in Pumbedita, too far apart to walk.
20.turn: The Gemara asks who carried them: Elijah, which would mean no Shabbat limit above ten handbreadths, or Yosef the demon.
20.outcome: Left open; the Gemara says it proves nothing since a demon could have done it.
20.summary: Seven teachings were said before Rav Ḥisda in Sura on Shabbat morning and then repeated before Rava in Pumbedita late that same Shabbat, a distance too far to walk. The Gemara asks if Elijah carried them through the air, but suggests a demon might have.
20.missing: The incident is only gestured at; who carried the teachings and how are never settled.
